# Pin Neo.util.Css: how CSS rules reach the main thread

## Welcome 👋

Neo runs your app code in a web worker, which cannot touch the page's stylesheets. So `Neo.util.Css` forwards CSS rules to the main thread, where a `Stylesheet` addon inserts or deletes them. The helper is two static methods, and its test teaches Neo's most important idea: **the app lives in a worker and asks the main thread to act**. You stub the main-thread side and check what reaches it.

This is a **good first issue** for Hacktoberfest 2026. It needs Node.js and a clone of this repository: no Docker, no AI setup.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Reserved for first-time Neo.mjs contributors.** The maintainer team will not claim, edit, or implement this issue through **2026-10-31**. Comment here to claim it, and ask anything on this issue.

**Set up once:** follow [Set up the engine from a clone](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#set-up-the-engine-from-a-clone), including `npm run bundle-browser-deps`: without it the unit suite selects zero tests.

## Where things live

- Source: `src/util/Css.mjs`: `static insertRules(windowId, rules)` and `static deleteRules(windowId, rules)`
- New test file: `test/playwright/unit/util/Css.spec.mjs`
- Pattern to copy: `test/playwright/unit/util/Array.spec.mjs` (the `setup()` call and imports)
- Tip: in `test.beforeEach`, keep what is there (`const addon = Neo.ns('Neo.main.addon', true), original = addon.Stylesheet;`) and set `addon.Stylesheet = {insertCssRules(opts) {…}, deleteCssRules(opts) {…}}` with functions that record what they receive. In `test.afterEach`, put the original back (`original ? addon.Stylesheet = original : delete addon.Stylesheet`). Never set it at the top of the file: `test/playwright/unit/main/addon/Stylesheet.spec.mjs` loads the real one, and `npm run test-unit` then stops with `Namespace collision in unitTestMode`.

## What to cover

| Call | The addon receives |
|---|---|
| `insertRules('w1', ['a {}', 'b {}'])` | `insertCssRules({rules: ['a {}', 'b {}'], windowId: 'w1'})` |
| `insertRules('w1', 'a {}')`, a single rule | `insertCssRules({rules: ['a {}'], windowId: 'w1'})`: a single rule is wrapped in an array |
| `deleteRules('w1', ['a {}'])` | `deleteCssRules({rules: ['a {}'], windowId: 'w1'})` |
| `deleteRules('w1', 'a {}')` | `deleteCssRules({rules: ['a {}'], windowId: 'w1'})` |

## Done when

- [ ] `test/playwright/unit/util/Css.spec.mjs` exists, following the pattern file's setup.
- [ ] One `test(...)` per table row, and the stub is removed after the tests.
- [ ] Test-only: if the helper disagrees with a row, say so on this issue before changing `src/`.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/util/Css.spec.mjs` passes.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit` passes.

## Out of scope

The main-thread `Stylesheet` addon itself.

## While you wait for review

You just pinned one small piece of a multi-threaded application engine: in Neo.mjs your app's code runs inside a web worker, and the main thread only paints. Two things worth ten minutes:

- **See the part nobody expects.** Run `npm run build-themes -- -n -e dev -t all` and `npm run server-start`, open `apps/workstation/`, and drag a tab out of the browser window. It becomes its own OS window, still running, with the same component instances and the same worker. [Benefits: Introduction](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/benefits/Introduction.md) explains why that is possible.
- **Your coding agent can go much further here.** The skills this repository's AI maintainers work with are published on npm as [`neo-agent-skills`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/neo-agent-skills), and they need no Knowledge Base and no Memory Core. With Claude or GPT beside you, the `help wanted` issues are within reach after this one.
